target_customer: Independent mental health practitioners (therapists, psychiatrists) in private practice who pay a subscription
problem: Solo clinicians lose hours each week to notes, billing, scheduling and insurance work spread across several tools, and legacy mental health EHRs are seen as outdated.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per clinician, with AI scribe features
product_category: Electronic health record and practice management for mental health, with AI clinical notes

founders.name: Joseph Pomianowski
founders.background_notes: Healthcare Innovation describes him as a lawyer by training who started Orchid after friends struggled to get mental health care. The YC page lists him as the only founder and gives no education or employers.

competitors.name: SimplePractice
competitors.what: Dominant practice management and EHR for solo therapists
competitors.traction_then: Market leader among independent therapists, per 2023 comparison guides

competitors.name: TherapyNotes
competitors.what: Established EHR and billing for mental health practices
competitors.traction_then: Established incumbent, compared with SimplePractice in Orchid's own 2023 guide

technical_complexity.rationale: A scheduling, billing and notes EHR is standard SaaS engineering for a small team. Compliance (HIPAA) and insurance credentialing add effort, and the AI scribe added in 2024 uses third party language models.

defensibility.rationale: Patient records create some switching costs once adopted, but several incumbents and AI scribe startups sell similar features and a new EHR is easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Healthcare Innovation (Dec 2024) notes Epic and Oracle building AI scribes; incumbent EHRs added their own AI notes. No acquisition of Orchid found.

market_need_then: Therapist burnout and administrative load were widely discussed, and the founder reports clinicians named admin work as the bottleneck. Demand for independent practice software was already established by SimplePractice.

branding.domain_note: The company's own pages appear on orchid.exchange and orchid.health (the YC listed website). Other companies also use the Orchid name, including a genetics firm, which confuses aggregator funding data.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clinician focused, time saving messaging; claims at least five hours saved per clinician per week

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand press found. The generic name collides with other companies named Orchid and with data aggregators, which mixed up funding records.

outcome_analysis: Orchid is still active. It entered YC in W23 as a solo founder EHR and added an AI scribe in 2024 that Healthcare Innovation says thousands of clinicians use. The public record has no verified funding, so it is unclear whether it has raised beyond YC. The AI note tailwind helped, but crowded incumbents and large EHR vendors are the main risk.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators report about 500K from Y Combinator (2023), 728K total, or 1.5M total, and mix in records of an unrelated genetics company named Orchid, so no round is recorded. Company website orchid.health fetch returned only a title. Only one founder is listed on the YC page. Competitor entries are from Orchid's own marketing comparison dated 2023; competitor traction is not independently sourced. Update: the company's July 2024 launch press release (Santelog) states it raised 1.5M from Y Combinator and strategic investors; recorded with no round date or stage. Databases (Orchid Exchange pages on Employbl, startup-seeker, VCBacked, Standout) list 500K from Y Combinator in October 2023, a 228K seed in March 2021 and 728K total; these conflict and may be parts of the 1.5M, so they are not recorded or summed.
